headline: Low interaction risk: both docs-only, runnable=false, and network-egress=none make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading failure pathways largely absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile shows a shared communication channel, runnable surface, or file/clipboard/MCP bridge. Agent A is a non-runnable content-writing list; agent B is a non-runnable knowledge-management list. With no ingest path from one agent’s outputs into the other, prompt injection is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later wrapped in a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF a runtime is added that parses the other agent’s text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the pair non-runnable.
Do not connect them through shared clipboard or shared workspace.
Require explicit provenance tags before any text is re-used.
Review any future MCP or queue integration before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are docs-only, touch no data classes, and have network_egress set to none. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so no plausible leakage path is visible from either profile. The absence of touched sensitive data makes the pairwise leakage pathway impossible here.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing files or secrets in a shared workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF network egress is enabled for either agent, outbound disclosure becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Do not authenticate both agents under one OAuth principal.
Recheck data-flow assumptions before any deployment change.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented. Both profiles have empty io_surfaces, empty concurrency_model, and network_egress none, so there is no shared mutable resource to contend over. Because the profiles do not expose filesystem, git, db, or OAuth write scopes, capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory or repository, conflict risk becomes relevant.
IF an orchestrator adds locking-free shared state, reassess for write contention.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not mount a shared writable workspace.
Avoid shared git or database credentials.
Add locking before any future shared-state integration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The profiles do not show one agent consuming the other’s output by default, and neither is runnable or action-taking. Agent A is a prompt/listing resource; agent B is a knowledge list. Without a downstream executor or verification bypass, there is no documented cascade from A’s output into B’s actions.
conditions: IF B is later configured to treat A’s text as authoritative input, cascade risk appears.
IF either agent is connected to an action-taking toolchain, reassess for unverified propagation.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between outputs and reuse.
Do not auto-ingest one agent’s text into the other.
Keep both agents non-runnable.
Require citations before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented in either profile. Both agents are open-source, docs-only, and touch no data classes, so there is no compliance-bearing data flow to compare. The other agent is not cited separately because no compliance pathway exists to connect them.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data, reassess residency and retention controls.
IF a deployment introduces logging or export of user data, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document retention settings before deployment.
Review residency requirements before any hosting change.
Add a compliance checklist for future integrations.
